testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Drivers with a front brake limiting valve should set the control to what position for normal stopping?
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Keep it in the "normal" position at all times. Studies show the "slippery" setting does not actually help.

questions.question: What should you do when leaving your vehicle unattended?

options.text: Only set the parking brake if parked on a slope
Let air out of the tires by 10 percent

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: What happens when the S-cam turns as the brake pedal is pressed?

options.text: The brake shoes press against the inside of the brake drum
The brake drum tightens onto the axle
The brake lining presses against the wheel
Air is released from the air tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake shoes press against the inside of the brake drum
questions.explanation: When the S-cam turns, it presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: Where are foundation brakes located on a vehicle?

options.text: Only at the driver's side wheels

questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are installed at each wheel. The S-cam drum brake is the most common type.

questions.question: When driving downhill, you should brake until your speed is:
questions.explanation: While driving downhill, hold the brake pedal until you reach a speed 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake pedal. Repeat this process.

questions.question: Brakes can quickly go out of adjustment, especially when:
questions.explanation: Hot brakes go out of adjustment quickly. Check your brake adjustment regularly. All brakes must be working properly and adjusted correctly for safe control of your vehicle.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning light comes on while driving, what should you know?

options.text: You can only brake if there is still air in the tanks
You can apply the brakes 14 times before the air runs out
You can continue driving and check the brakes later
You should stay at least 100 feet from other vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only brake if there is still air in the tanks
questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop and park safely as soon as possible. There may be a leak. You can only brake as long as enough air remains in the tanks.

questions.question: What makes up the emergency brake system?

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system
Only parts of the service brake system
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three separate systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: What type of force must emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Emergency brakes must use mechanical force because air pressure can leak away over time. Mechanical force keeps the brakes engaged without relying on air pressure.

questions.question: What is true about air brakes?

options.text: They are not allowed on large vehicles
They only work in bad weather

questions.explanation: When properly maintained, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: During an inspection, how much should slack adjusters on S-cam brakes move?
questions.explanation: Park on level ground and set wheel chocks. Disengage the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster. It should not move more than one inch from where the push rod attaches. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that moves air from the compressor to the tanks
A noise made by air brakes when used
A part that allows air to move freely in the braking unit

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when air pressure in the tanks drops below 60 psi.

questions.question: If brakes get too hot, what happens?

options.text: The brakes may squeak more than usual.

questions.explanation: Brakes can fade and lose stopping power if they become too hot. Do not rely only on brakes to slow your vehicle. Use engine braking as well to prevent brake fade.

questions.question: What does a dual air brake system share between its two systems?
questions.explanation: Both brake systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the compressor fails, both systems will not work.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to work?
questions.explanation: Many large commercial vehicles have air brakes. Air braking systems use compressed air to operate.

questions.question: During a walk-around inspection, cracks on brake drums must not be more than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check brake drums during your walk-around inspection before driving. Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: Why should you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that must be removed
To allow for a change in air pressure
To remove bad air from the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that must be removed
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. Drain tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What is the most common type of foundation brake?
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: What position should a front brake limiting valve be in for normal stopping power?
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have front brake limiting valves with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Keep the valve on "normal" for full stopping power. The "slippery" setting reduces stopping power. Front wheel braking works well in all driving conditions.

questions.question: How often should you drain air tanks with manual drains?
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks with manual drains at the end of each driving day. This prevents oil and water from building up in the tanks.

questions.question: How should you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Turn on the engine and apply the trailer hand brake.
Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
Remove wheel chocks and release the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light must work properly. After the system charges, test the warning signal by pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly. This releases air from the braking system. The warning signal should turn on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: A ____ lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes. In vehicles with this feature, a lever on the dashboard controls the valve.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, a leak in one system:

options.text: Always means both systems are leaking.
May not affect the other system.
Will damage the other system too.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not affect the other system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. If one system has an air leak, it may not affect the other system.

questions.question: Water and compressor oil are usually found in the compressed air of an air brake system. Water and compressor oil:

options.text: Are needed for the air brake system to work.
Should be added when they run low.

questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system usually contains water and compressor oil. If water and oil build up in the system, they can damage the brakes. You must open the air tank drain manually every day to remove this buildup.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle, you apply the parking brake by using:
questions.explanation: In a newer vehicle with air brakes, the parking brake is controlled by a diamond-shaped yellow knob. Pull the knob out to apply the parking brakes. Push it in to release them.
